schema_lineage.purpose: AI TRiSM evaluation schema with research methodology documentation, rationale consolidation logic, and comprehensive field mapping

ai_trism_taxonomy_v1.1.intent: Evaluate vendors and platforms on their AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) capabilities. Scores reflect the maturity, specificity, measurability, and autonomy of AI-enabled TRiSM controls—not the general product capability. This version documents the complete research pipeline, rationale consolidation methodology, and all data fields used in vendor scoring.

metadata.framework_alignment: Gartner AI TRiSM layers (Gov/Runtime/InfoGov) + NIST AI RMF + ISO/IEC 42001

scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of AI-enabled TRiSM capability in this area

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No publicly verifiable evidence of AI-enabled TRiSM in this capability.
scoring_logic.1: No AI/ML: Policy/process or manual controls only; no AI-based enforcement, monitoring, or evaluation beyond simple rules/scripting.
scoring_logic.2: Generic AI Claims: Marketing mentions AI/ML guardrails but lacks named models, policy engines, runtime hooks, metrics, or docs.
scoring_logic.3: AI-Augmented: Documented AI models or policy engines assist humans (e.g., runtime detections, cataloging, or evaluations) with human approval gates; some use-case specifics disclosed.
scoring_logic.4: Advanced AI: Named models/policy engines with measurable outcomes (block/allow rates, false-positive/negative, latency). Partially automated runtime enforcement with blended risk scoring; continuous assurance pipelines.
scoring_logic.5: Fully Agentic: Autonomous TRiSM controls that plan, inspect, enforce, and auto-remediate within governance bounds; full auditability of AI actions, versioned models, error rates, and override points disclosed.

source_policy.description: Evidence must be publicly accessible and verifiable; not restricted to vendor domains.
invalid_sources: Generic sales collateral without technical detail

research_methodology.pipeline_overview: The TRiSM research pipeline progresses through versioned stages. Each stage enriches vendor records with additional data and refines scores based on evidence. No stage deletes prior data; each appends new layers.

v1_0_seed.description: Initial vendor list with raw pillar/sub-pillar scores from capability claims. No evidence validation.

v1_1_validated.description: Validate vendor existence, websites, and basic claims. Produce validated scores and rationale strings.

v2_0_researched.description: Deep research: fetch public evidence, evaluate against schema criteria, produce structured rationale objects with evidence quality analysis and score adjustments.

v2_1_consolidated.description: Data-only transform: consolidate three rationale sources (score_rationale, evidence_quality_rationale, score_adjustment.reason) plus criteria assessment into a single human-readable string per sub-pillar. No external fetches.

inputs.description: Primary scoring justification: why this maturity level was assigned, evidence basis (excerpt count, source count, term matches), criteria met/partial/unmet, and evidence specificity.
Evidence quality grade (A-F) with breakdown: source diversity factor, volume assessment, term specificity, cross-source confirmation, and schema criteria coverage ratio.
Explanation of why the score was adjusted from its original (v1) value, including the analytical level determination and evidence strength comparison.

additional_context_included.description: Array of per-criterion evaluations with status (met/partial/unmet), supporting evidence text, and confidence level.
Top evidence snippets used in the scoring decision.

consolidation_logic.output_format: Human-readable text with labeled sections: [Score Rationale], [Evidence Quality], [Score Adjustment], [Criteria Assessment], [Key Evidence]

rationale_consolidation_logic.description: The v2.1 consolidated rationale merges three independent analytical outputs into one readable field per sub-pillar. This is the authoritative rationale for display in the vendor detail modal.

section_1_score_rationale.content: States the assigned score, maturity level label, evidence strength indicators (coverage %, V1 signal correlation, pillar term matches, schema criteria matches), and lists criteria that are fully met, partially met, or unmet with specific gap descriptions.
section_1_score_rationale.example_prefix: Vendor scores X.XX/5.0 (Level N: Label). Evidence: coverage=XX%, V1 signal=X.XX...

section_2_evidence_quality.content: Assigns a letter grade (A-F) to the evidence base. Breaks down: source diversity factor (0-1), excerpt volume, term specificity, cross-source confirmation, and schema criteria coverage ratio. Low grades flag unreliable scores.
section_2_evidence_quality.example_prefix: Evidence quality: XX.X% — Grade X (Label). Source diversity...

section_3_score_adjustment.content: Explains score movement from original (v1) to adjusted (v2). Includes direction (increased/decreased/confirmed), magnitude, and the analytical reasoning (criteria met count, key evidence count, analytical level).
section_3_score_adjustment.example_prefix: X.XX → X.XX: Score decreased/confirmed — rationale analysis...

section_4_criteria_assessment.content: Per-criterion breakdown with status icons (✅ met, ⚠️ partial, ❌ unmet) and the criterion text. Provides a quick summary line (N met, N partial, N unmet of N total).

section_5_key_evidence.content: Top 3 evidence snippets (150 chars each) that were most influential in the scoring decision.

GOV.name: AI Governance
GOV.focus: Visibility, accountability, and continuous assurance across all AI entities and use cases.
ai_evidence_signals: AI catalog with risk scores across models, agents, and apps
AI data mapping/lineage tied to each AI entity
Automated documentation, audit trails, and approvals/attestations
Continuous assurance: evaluations, red-teaming, posture & compliance dashboards

RUN.name: Runtime Inspection & Enforcement
RUN.focus: Single-pass, low-latency runtime controls that inspect inputs/outputs/activities and enforce enterprise policy.
ai_evidence_signals: Unified runtime policy engines with blended risk scoring
Context-aware data protection (dynamic classification, PBAC, selective redaction)

INF.name: Information Governance (for AI)
INF.focus: Data discovery, classification, access control, retention, and PETs to prevent oversharing and data compromise.
ai_evidence_signals: DSPM/DLP/DAG controls across SaaS, cloud, productivity suites
Policy of least privilege/PBAC; permissions hygiene at scale
PETs: masking, tokenization, synthetic data, confidential compute
Cross-functional operating model integrations (Security, D&A, IAM, Compliance)

GOV-01.name: AI Catalog & Inventory
GOV-01.expanded_definition: Discovery and risk scoring of all AI entities (models, agents, apps), including ownership, lineage, and life-cycle state.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated discovery of embedded and homegrown AI entities
Risk scoring per entity with policy/control coverage mapping
Owner/approver attribution and versioned lifecycle records
Searchable registry with model cards/BOMs and runtime metrics
APIs to export catalog and integrate with SIEM/GRC

GOV-02.name: AI Data Mapping & Lineage
GOV-02.expanded_definition: Map training, fine-tuning, RAG, and agent context data to each AI entity and maintain lineage over time.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated mapping of data sets to specific AI entities
Lineage tracking (provenance, transformations, access history)
Data quality & sensitivity labeling tied to AI usage
Impact analysis for dataset changes on governed AI entities
Interfaces with data catalogs/MDM for bidirectional sync

GOV-03.name: Documentation, Audit & Approvals
GOV-03.expanded_definition: Automated generation and maintenance of model cards, audit trails, approvals/attestations, and third-party RFI workflows.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated documentation (model cards, BOM, reports)
Immutable audit trails of AI artifacts and state changes
Workflow for approvals/exceptions with evidence attachments
Third-party AI RFI/evidence exchange and validation
Compliance mapping to NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / EU AI Act

GOV-04.name: Continuous Assurance & Posture
GOV-04.expanded_definition: Pre- and post-deployment evaluations, red teaming, risk/control validation, and compliance reporting.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated red teaming (prompt attacks, adversarial tests) with results back to risk posture
Continuous policy/control validation (bias, leakage, trust, alignment)
Runtime metrics feeding posture dashboards and alerts
Compliance reporting with evidence links and trend views
APIs for SIEM/SOAR/GRC integration

RUN-01.name: Unified Runtime Control Plane
RUN-01.expanded_definition: Single-pass inspection with multiple policy engines (safety, legal/compliance, security) and blended risk scoring.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Parallel policy engines with aggregated risk/decisioning
Latency SLAs and throughput benchmarks documented
Deterministic escalation routes by violation class
Pluggable policies/models; provider-agnostic connectors
Evidence of reduced conflicts vs siloed controls

RUN-02.name: Security & Threat Defense
RUN-02.expanded_definition: Detection and prevention of prompt injection, jailbreaks, adversarial inputs, and anomalous model/agent behavior.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Prompt-injection/jailbreak detection with measurable block rates
Model/app/agent monitoring for anomalous activities
Signature + ML hybrid techniques for robustness
Auto-remediation playbooks with rollback
Feeds to SIEM/SOAR for incident response

RUN-03.name: Safety, Quality & Compliance Filtering
RUN-03.expanded_definition: Input/output checking for toxicity, IP/copyright, hallucinations, and regulatory/policy violations with explainer artifacts.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Content anomaly detection with precision/recall metrics
Hallucination & factuality checks with citations
IP/copyright filters and licensing policy enforcement
Regulatory templates (e.g., EU AI Act risk class checks)
Explainability artifacts (rationales, scores, evidence IDs)

RUN-04.name: Contextual Data Protection at Runtime
RUN-04.expanded_definition: Dynamic classification, PBAC/least-privilege enforcement, and selective redaction/obfuscation in transit.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Dynamic content classification inline with AI sessions
PBAC/ABAC enforcement bound to user/app/agent purpose
Selective redaction/tokenization with low latency
Per-transaction data access logs and alerts
Integration with DSPM/DLP/IAM to adjust permissions

INF-01.name: Data Discovery & Classification
INF-01.expanded_definition: Discover and classify sensitive data across SaaS, cloud, and productivity platforms relevant to AI.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated discovery across structured/unstructured stores
ML-driven classifiers for sensitivity and ownership
Coverage metrics and blind-spot detection
Linkage to AI use cases/RAG indexes
Bulk remediation workflows

INF-02.name: Access Governance & Sharing Hygiene
INF-02.expanded_definition: Permissions hygiene at scale with least-privilege/PBAC and lifecycle (retention/ROT) enforcement.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Automated permission right-sizing recommendations
PBAC policies bound to AI purposes and contexts
Lifecycle policies (retention, ROT cleanup) with evidence
Alerting on oversharing hotspots relevant to AI copilots
Change impact simulations before enforcement

INF-03.name: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs)
INF-03.expanded_definition: Apply PETs across training, tuning, inference, and agentic workflows.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Runtime masking/redaction/tokenization with rehydration controls
Synthetic data/differential privacy for evaluations
Confidential computing/TEEs for sensitive workloads
Documented privacy risk reduction metrics
Governed key/secret management for AI contexts

INF-04.name: Cross-Functional Operating Model
INF-04.expanded_definition: Coordination across Security, D&A, Digital Workplace, IAM, and Compliance to sustain InfoGov for AI at scale.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Documented RACI and workflows for AI data access changes
Joint KPIs (oversharing reduction, MTTR for policy fixes)
Integrated change mgmt from detection → permission fix
TTX for InfoGov failure modes (e.g., oversharing in copilots)
Evidence of scaled adoption in M365/Workspace estates
